slice.leaf: Inspect exactly the rmcp-v3.1.4 task model types needed by an application-owned persistent task handler: GetTaskResult, DetailedTask, GetTaskParams, CancelTaskParams, and UpdateTaskParams constructors, fields, and serde wire names.

GetTaskParams.serde: rename_all=camelCase; meta explicitly renamed _meta and omitted when None

CancelTaskParams.serde: rename_all=camelCase; meta explicitly renamed _meta and omitted when None

UpdateTaskParams.serde: rename_all=camelCase; meta explicitly renamed _meta and omitted when None

Task.important_serde_detail: ttlMs serializes as null when None; statusMessage and pollIntervalMs are omitted when None

DetailedTask.wire: base Task fields flattened at top level; payload is also top-level and selected by status: working/cancelled carry no extra field, input_required requires inputRequests, completed requires result, failed requires error

GetTaskResult.wire: resultType and optional _meta plus DetailedTask flattened at top level
GetTaskResult.serde: rename_all=camelCase; result_type defaults on deserialize; meta explicitly renamed _meta; task flattened

minimal_override_data_contract.adapter_implication: A custom persistent task backend can rehydrate a stored row into Task::new(...) plus optional setters, combine it with a status-specific TaskPayload via DetailedTask::new(...), and return GetTaskResult::new(...). Get/cancel/update request decoding can rely on the SDK constructors and serde names above rather than hand-maintaining alternate wire keys. Because the structs are non_exhaustive, external application code should prefer these constructors over struct literals where available.
minimal_override_data_contract.persistence_minimum: To reconstruct tasks/get exactly, storage must retain taskId, status, createdAt, lastUpdatedAt, nullable ttlMs, optional statusMessage/pollIntervalMs, and the status-specific payload needed by DetailedTask (inputRequests/result/error as applicable).
